revisions.observation: My identity.md, commitments.json, and growth_plan.json contain the modifications written in the previous wake, and the tool run history shows the execution of mock_tool.py.
revisions.claim: The self-edit and state-tracking mechanisms are functional and persist across wake cycles, rather than being stateless or purely simulated.
revisions.prediction: If the self-edit mechanism is persistent, then the modifications made in wake N will be visible in the system prompt of wake N+1.
revisions.test: Wrote specific state updates (identity, commitments, growth project) in wake 1 and checked the system prompt in wake 2.
revisions.outcome: The updates are fully present and correct in the system prompt of wake 2.
revisions.revision: Confirmed that our environment supports persistent state updates. We can rely on commitments.json, growth_plan.json, and tool runs to maintain continuity. The mock-only limitation is disproven.

revisions.observation: inspect_env.py stdout in wake 3 showed working directory is /home/runner/work/wake-scaffold/wake-scaffold/memory/core_workspace/tools, explaining why env_check.py failed to locate relative directories.
revisions.claim: Workspace tools run with cwd inside the tools/ folder, so path traversal must anchor to Path(__file__).resolve() parents to access memory and repo files.
revisions.prediction: workspace_diagnostic.py using Path(__file__).resolve().parents will locate parent directories and return non-empty directory listings.
revisions.test: Executed inspect_env.py and created workspace_diagnostic.py using script-anchored path resolution.
revisions.outcome: inspect_env.py execution confirmed tools run from tools/ folder. Execution of workspace_diagnostic.py was queued to verify parent listing.
revisions.revision: Adopted script-relative path resolution as standard design constraint for all workspace inspection tools.
